Sample.evidence_source: The text provides Ns for T1, T2, and T3 (294, 282, 202 respectively) but does not report any subjective well-being components (life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect) for which these Ns would apply.

infoYearT1.evidence_source: The current study used data from a multi-site longitudinal study examining risk-factors for psychopathology within youth (Hankin et al., 2015). ... The current study examined participants' responses at three time points: T1, T2 (18-months post-T1) and T3 (30-months post-T1). Within the larger longitudinal study, T1 corresponded to the 18-month follow-up, T2 corresponded to the 36-month follow-up and T3 represented the 48-month follow-up.

country.evidence_source: Specifically, a 48-month assessment was conducted exclusively at the Denver site. Thus, the current sample represents participants recruited from the Greater Denver area only.

Outcome_variable.evidence_source: The text mentions 'depression' and 'anxiety symptoms' in the context of retention analysis, but does not report any subjective well-being measures (life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect).

sample_type.evidence_source: Participants of the larger longitudinal study were initially recruited via brief informational letters sent to families within the broader Denver area. Caregivers with a child in third, sixth or ninth grade then contacted the university to be scheduled for a baseline visit.

ethnicity.evidence_source: For ethnicity, 11% reported being Latinx; for race, youth indicated the following: 75.4% White, 6.8% African American, 3.6% Asian/Pacific Islander, 1% American Indian/Alaskan Native, 6.5% more than one race and 6.8% Other.

lag.evidence_source: The current study examined participants' responses at three time points: T1, T2 (18-months post-T1) and T3 (30-months post-T1).
lag.warning: The intervals between waves are 18 months (T1-T2) and 12 months (T2-T3), which are not consistent. Therefore, a single 'typical' lag cannot be determined.
